overall_reason: The content is specific and only-this-product (draw.mjs and its 20 named directions, CC-licensed picture credits, the inspector's FAIL list, the Bohne & Söhne example builds), but it sits in a stock wrapper: dark-to-orange glow hero with an announcement pill, sponsor cells, eyebrowed alternating feature cards, FAQ, a 'Stop guessing, start deciding.' CTA band and a link footer.

findings.evidence: Full-bleed gradient from near-black #140a05 to #ff5b14 with a radial 'sun' glow (#ff9652, alpha 0.62) under centred white text; saturated accent covers 46% of the fold (sweep). The glow carries no information about the skill.
findings.before: Centred h1 over a sunset gradient and glow
findings.after: Lead with the example builds (the Coffee shop / Club night / Architects / Contracts previews visible at 375) on a flat ground; let the product be the hero image.
findings.why: Mirror test: the centred-text-over-glowing-gradient hero is what a neighbouring dev-tool brief gets; it is the one decision that makes the first screen read as default.

findings.evidence: Pair and fragment formula repeats: 'look designed, not generated', 'Twenty directions. Three dealt per page.', 'Design sense, packaged as a skill.', 'From default to designed.', 'Common questions.', 'Stop guessing, start deciding.'
findings.after: Say what the command does: "Install it and your next page starts from one of twenty directions."
findings.why: Over-correction: the page avoids buzzwords but replaces them with the clipped two-beat cadence; 'Stop guessing, start deciding' passes the rival-name swap for any product.

findings.evidence: Section order from dom-1440: announcement pill + centred hero, sponsor logo cells, 'The draw', 'How it works' three alternating feature cards, before/after, install tabs, TasteCode promo, FAQ 'Common questions.', sponsor wall, CTA band, 3-column link footer. Stock items present: logo strip, equal feature cards, FAQ, CTA band, link-farm footer (5).
findings.before: Stock landing order around the specific middle
findings.after: Cut the CTA band and the second sponsor block; move 'The draw' directly under the hero, since it is the idea only this product has.
findings.why: Five stock sections in stock order make the frame read as a template even though the middle is specific.

findings.evidence: Small orange label above every heading: 'The draw', 'How it works', 'Pictures', 'Inspector', 'App screens', 'Before and after', 'Install', 'Questions', 'Open source'.
findings.before: Pictures / Finds real pictures and credits them
findings.after: Drop the labels; the headings already name the feature ('Finds real pictures and credits them').
findings.why: An eyebrow on every block is template rhythm; each label restates its heading.

findings.evidence: Announcement pill 'TasteCode is out: Taste Skill as a desktop app →' centred above the h1.
findings.after: Move the TasteCode news into the nav or the TasteCode section further down.
findings.why: The news pill over a centred h1 is the default hero kit; it pushes the real claim down.

strengths: 'The draw': twenty named directions ('The name as a monument', 'Fintech as streetwear', 'The dark room') with plain glosses; nothing else in the category says this.

Concrete, falsifiable claims: '247 curated sites', 'Openverse, Wikimedia Commons, the Art Institute of Chicago and the Met. Only CC0, public domain, CC BY and CC BY-SA', 'Roughly 30 to 45 minutes and a few hundred thousand tokens'.
The example builds (Bohne & Söhne, Leipzig) and the inspector's FAIL/WARN list show the product working rather than describing it.
Honest footer lines: 'Taste Skill has no token or coin.', photo credits.
not_investigated: disputed: sweep SLP-012 violet-gradient family and the 'Revolutionize', 'Unlock', 'cutting-edge', 'seamless' lexicon hits come from the 'NoteFlow' demo inside 'Before and after', which is labelled 'The default ... The page every agent ships': a quoted bad example, not the page's own look or copy.

Large parts of the 1440 capture are blank (tiles 03, 04, 09, 10, 11; sweep dead_band and hidden_content 81% when IntersectionObserver never fires): judged from dom-1440 text and the 375 tiles; one script chunk was blocked (manifest network).
